sections.h2: Filing a deed with Allegan County
sections.html:
Paper and electronic filing both work. The register's page lists three e-recording vendors with direct lines: CSC (866-652-0111), Simplifile (800-460-5657) and ePN, the E-Recording Partners Network (888-325-3365). Title companies normally use one of these, which spares most sellers any contact with them. The register's phone is 269-673-0390.

The same page links a land records search portal and the state recording requirements. After filing, the register enters the paper in a book called a liber and stamps that reference on the document. An image becomes the permanent record, and the office does not keep the original deed or mortgage.

Counter staff do not prepare documents or answer legal questions, and they refer people to an attorney or title company. One protection for senders comes from MCL 565.201: a register may not refuse a compliant paper over its wording, and a paper already recorded is presumed to comply. The format rules are the real hurdle, so let the title agent look over the deed before signing.

One flat $30 covers a recording of any length, as MCL 600.2567 provides. The remaining items on the statutory list are short.

  • $3 on top for every further instrument that a single paper assigns or discharges.
  • $1 per page of copies, and a $5 certification charge.
  • Grantor and grantee searches at 50 cents per year examined, minimum $5.
  • $1 for filing or looking up any other paper.

Fees are due when the paper is left. For electronic filings the fee can follow electronically, up to one business day after receipt. For copy purposes, a "page" is one side of a sheet measuring 8 1/2 by 11 up to 14 inches, in paper of 20 pound weight or more.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax is due on an Allegan County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays two taxes that together come to $4.30 for each $500 of value, rounding a partial $500 upward.

Transfer tax rates on an Allegan County sale
LevelRate per $500Paid by
County$0.55Seller
State$3.75Seller
Combined$4.30Seller

The seller carries liability under MCL 207.523, although a buyer may pay on the seller's behalf. Payment reaches the county treasurer no later than 15 days after the instrument is delivered. Ask the title agent to show the tax on your settlement statement before you sign.

sections.h2: Which transfers can skip the tax?
sections.html:
MCL 207.526 exempts a list of transfers, and a few come up often with houses in a lake or farm county like this one.

  • A deed that only straightens a boundary line when no money changes hands.
  • A quitclaim deed given to confirm a title the grantee already holds, such as one that corrects a flaw.
  • A transfer between a limited liability company and its members when ownership shares are unchanged.
  • A transfer between a partnership and its partners on the same terms.
  • A deed in which the grantor is a government body or officer acting officially.

Anyone relying on one of these should say so to the title agent before closing. A refund request goes to the Department of Treasury.

The office runs a free Property Fraud Alert. An owner or business enters a name and gets a notice whenever a recorded document matches it, which gives early warning of a forged deed or a lien filed against you.

The register also posts Plat Board public notices, which matter to anyone splitting a parcel before a sale. A related treasurer form covers tax certification for land divisions and lot line adjustments, with its own instructions.

U.S. passport applications are taken at the office by appointment only, between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays.

sections.h2: What does the Allegan County Treasurer handle in a sale?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's Office certifies deeds, keeps tax histories, and collects delinquent real estate tax for the 35 townships, cities and villages in the county. The county runs the whole tax reversion process in-house, including title searches, court hearings, foreclosure and sale.

A seller with delinquent tax should talk to the treasurer's staff first, because the office advances delinquent amounts to the local units through its revolving fund. The treasurer's pages link to pay delinquent taxes, search tax records and view foreclosure sales.

Former owners can also claim leftover foreclosure proceeds. A person with title or equity files Form 5743 with the county treasurer by July 1 of the foreclosure year. The county replies by January 31 after the auctions with Form 5744, and a court motion may follow between February 1 and May 15. These steps come from MCL 211.78t.

sections.h2: Who sets and bills property tax?
sections.html:
Assessing happens at the township or city level. The county Equalization Department publishes property records, a list of township and city assessors, equalization reports and a tax levies and millages page.

Because 24 townships, 9 cities and 2 villages each act as their own unit, the correct office depends on the parcel. The county directory lists addresses and phone lines for all of them, such as Allegan Township at 269-673-5051, Otsego City Hall at 269-692-3391 and Holland City Hall at 616-355-1300.

Ask your township or city for the current tax balance before you list the house.

The county seat is the city of Allegan, and Holland is the largest city. The Lake Michigan shore draws vacation homes, especially around Saugatuck and Douglas, and much of the inland area is farmland. The 2025 population estimate is 123,188, and owners live in 87.4 percent of homes.

Many sellers here own lakeshore cottages, second homes or farm parcels. Those often involve a survey, a land division or an old tax history, so check with the township about splits before you list, and ask the treasurer about tax certification when a parcel is divided.

sections.h2: Steps for an Allegan County seller
sections.html:
1. Ask your township or city for the current tax balance.
  2. Have the title agent review the deed against the state format rules.
  3. Choose paper or e-recording. Most title companies use CSC, Simplifile or ePN.
  4. Pay the $30 recording fee and any add-ons, then the transfer tax within 15 days.
  5. Turn on the free Property Fraud Alert so you hear about any later filing in your name.

If the house has delinquent tax, call the treasurer before you set a closing date. A cash as-is sale can fit when you need a firm date, and any offer is yours to decline. Keep your recorded deed image and the liber reference, since the office does not hold the original paper.

faqs.q: Which e-recording services does Allegan County accept?
faqs.a: It accepts CSC, Simplifile and ePN. Their phone lines are 866-652-0111, 800-460-5657 and 888-325-3365.

faqs.q: How much does a deed cost to record in Allegan County?
faqs.a: A recording costs $30 per document. Add $3 per further instrument assigned or discharged, $1 a page for copies and $5 for certification.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on an Allegan County sale?
faqs.a: The seller is liable, at $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state. A buyer may pay on the seller's behalf, and payment goes to the county treasurer within 15 days.

faqs.q: Will the Allegan County register prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office neither drafts documents nor answers legal questions, so an attorney or title company must do that.

faqs.q: How does a former owner claim surplus from an Allegan County foreclosure sale?
faqs.a: Send Form 5743 to the county treasurer by July 1 of the foreclosure year. The county replies by January 31 with Form 5744, and a court motion may follow.
